item.title: CPC plenum concludes, adopting resolution on persevering with full, rigorous Party self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 23:55:00
Top News The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) held its fifth plenary session from Monday to Thursday in Beijing, adopting a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee presided over the meeting. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered an important address, said a communique issued after the session, per the Xinhua News Agency. According to the communique issued after the session, the meeting adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. Chinese experts said the fifth plenary session underscores the CPC's determination to strengthen internal discipline and sustain its anti-corruption campaign, while reinforcing the Party's capacity to govern at a critical stage in China's development. The experts stressed that the greatest threats to a ruling party can come from within, making sustained self-governance and strict internal discipline essential to avoiding the historical cycle of rise and decline. Moreover, as China advances its modernization drive, the session carries broader significance for maintaining policy continuity, strengthening governance and laying the groundwork for the country's long-term development. Rigorous self-governance At the session, the CPC Central Committee gave a highly positive assessment of the great achievements the Party has made in exercising full and rigorous self-governance in the new era. It was pointed out that as the Party endeavors to supervise, govern, develop, and strengthen itself in the new era, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking, and new strategies in response to the major questions of the times -- what kind of long-term governing Marxist party the CPC should build and how to build it, thereby giving rise to Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. "It was stressed that many favorable conditions are now in place for advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, while we also face many new circumstances and new issues in this endeavor," the communique said. Profound changes in global, national, and Party conditions have made the CPC's tasks of uniting and leading the people in safeguarding China's sovereignty, security, and development interests, of uniting and leading the people in promoting reform and development and maintaining social harmony and stability, and of maintaining its advanced nature and integrity even more formidable, it added. At the session, the guiding principles for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were highlighted as follows: serving the Party's missions and tasks; taking strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle; exercising rigorous governance across the board; adopting a problem-oriented approach; upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground; adhering to a top-down approach; and running the Party according to regulations. Systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were also made at the session with the emphasis on strengthening the Party spirit of Communists; strictly practicing democratic centralism; cultivating high-caliber officials capable of shouldering the mission of national rejuvenation; building a well-knit organizational system characterized by cross-level alignment and effective implementation; improving conduct and tightening discipline on an ongoing basis; taking firm and coordinated action against corruption; running the Party with systems and regulations; refining Party and state oversight systems; and ensuring all responsibilities of Party self-supervision and self-governance are fulfilled in earnest, according to the communique. Strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance, it noted. Party organizations at all levels play the principal role in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique, adding that it is therefore essential to systematically advance the development of Party organizations at all levels and in all sectors to strengthen their political and organizational functions. Improving conduct and tightening discipline are effective measures to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique. "It was noted that taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption is both an important strategy for full and rigorous Party self-governance and a fundamental guideline for our fight against corruption," the communique said. "We must take systematic steps to address both symptoms and root causes of corruption and adopt a holistic approach that combines severe punishment, targeted remedy, and effective prevention, carrying this fight through to the end," it stated. The purpose of strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance is to make the Communist Party of China (CPC) stronger, Xin Ming, a professor at the School of Marxism, Beihang University, told the Global Times. He noted that the strength comes from continuous self-reform and self-improvement, rooting out problems that undermine the Party's health, so that it can remain vigorous and better fulfill its responsibilities and missions. Advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance is also a process of ensuring that the CPC stays true to its founding mission of serving the people, enabling it to pursue the long-term interests of society rather than catering to particular groups for short-term gains or yielding to external interference, Chen Shu, a professor from the Party School of the CPC Central Committee, told the Global Times. Chen noted that the greatest threats often come from within, stressing that maintaining strict internal discipline is essential to overcoming the historical cycle of rise and decline and ensuring lasting stability. General Secretary Xi has led an unprecedented anti-corruption campaign since 2012, driven by a determination to "offend a few thousand rather than fail 1.4 billion." The campaign has targeted corrupt officials at both high and low levels, according to a Xinhua report. An official review of work in 2025 reported that disciplinary and supervisory bodies nationwide investigated 967,000 cases of misconduct and corruption affecting people's daily lives, returning or helping recover about 77.6 billion yuan ($11.5 billion) in money and property to the public. Far-reaching significance Studying and implementing the guiding principles from this plenary session represent a major political task for the entire Party both at present and in the period to come, according to the communique. It was also stressed that all aspects of the Party's work agenda should be steadily advanced at the turn of the year. The CPC Central Committee decided at the session that the Party will convene its 21st National Congress in Beijing in the second half of 2027 and stated that this congress, which is to be held at a critical stage for basically realizing socialist modernization and on a new journey toward the Second Centenary Goal, will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country. The session elected Zhang Shengmin as a new member of the CPC Central Committee Political Bureau, according to the communique. The session also decided on the filling of empty seats on the Central Committee by alternate members, deliberated and adopted inspection reports of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the Central Military Commission on those committing grave violations of discipline and laws, and confirmed the Political Bureau's previous decisions to punish those violators. The CPC Central Committee called upon the entire Party to rally more closely around the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core and fully implement Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. As China enters a critical phase of its modernization drive, the fifth plenary session's emphasis on tightening Party discipline and strengthening internal governance is of particular significance. Achieving the goals and tasks of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) requires a particular focus on improving the Party's capacity and competence in steering economic and social development, analysts said. The CPC's capacity to mobilize society and sustain long-term development has rested on its political leadership, policy planning and institutional framework. Strengthening the Party's capacity to govern is crucial to carrying out China's long-term development agenda, Xin noted.

item.title: China to continue suspending export quota management for phosphate rock, silver in 2027; policy facilitates compliant trade while retaining regulatory oversight
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 23:41:00
China's Ministry of Commerce Photo: Yin Yeping/GT China will continue to suspend export quota management for phosphate rock and silver while maintaining export licensing requirements, according to the 2027 export quota arrangements released by China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) on Thursday, extending a policy in place since 2019 that an industry analyst said reflects China's commitment to facilitating legitimate trade in critical minerals, rather than using its resource advantages to restrict global supplies. The arrangement comes as critical minerals, including phosphate and silver, attract growing international attention for their importance to advanced manufacturing and the energy transition. Under the arrangements, eligible exporters of phosphate rock or silver may apply for export licenses with valid export contracts and use the licenses to complete customs declarations and clearance procedures. The policy adjustment first took effect on January 1, 2019, as part of efforts to improve China's export management system and streamline administrative procedures, according to an earlier MOFCOM announcement. It has since been maintained in subsequent years. The two commodities have gained prominence in discussions over critical mineral supply chains. In November 2025, the US Geological Survey added phosphate and silver to its updated list of 60 critical minerals, reflecting their growing economic and strategic importance. Silver, a precious metal with both financial and industrial applications, is playing an increasingly important role in emerging industries, with demand driven by sectors including solar power and new-energy vehicles, according to the Xinhua News Agency. Phosphate rock, meanwhile, is a crucial raw material for fertilizer production and the manufacturing of lithium iron phosphate batteries, which are widely used in electric vehicles and energy storage systems. China has also maintained measures to facilitate exports of other critical minerals. Under its 2026 export licensing rules, the country continued to suspend designated-port requirements for exports of rare earths, magnesia, antimony, and related products. The longstanding measures allow exporters to choose ports based on logistics costs, delivery times, and market needs, helping streamline shipments and improve customs clearance efficiency, industry observers said. Stable and predictable management Wu Chenhui, an independent analyst who closely follows the critical minerals industry, told the Global Times that China's decision to maintain the longstanding arrangement reflects policy continuity and a differentiated approach to managing strategically important resources. Critical minerals carry considerable economic and strategic importance, but managing their exports does not necessarily mean restricting normal trade, nor does China seek to use such measures to leverage its resource advantages to pressure other countries, Wu said. The distinction between export quotas and export licensing is particularly important, according to the analyst. Unlike a quota system, which allocates a limited export volume among eligible businesses, the licensing arrangement allows qualified exporters to apply for licenses based on actual contracts without being subject to an annual export quota for the two commodities. This can reduce the uncertainty associated with quota allocation, give companies greater flexibility in arranging shipments and help stabilize expectations among overseas customers, Wu said. China's approach also stands in contrast to the tendency in some overseas discussions to treat critical mineral export management as synonymous with supply restrictions. The arrangement retains necessary regulatory procedures while facilitating legitimate trade, showing that resource management and smoother international commerce are not mutually exclusive, he added. China's silver exports reached around 5,100 tons in 2025, the highest level in at least 16 years, Bloomberg reported in January, despite the continuation of its export licensing regime. The MOFCOM has also approved 44 companies to export silver in 2026-27, two more than in 2025, although exporters remain subject to qualification requirements. The figures suggest that the continuation of licensing rules has not prevented silver exports from reaching record levels. Cooperation over confrontation China's management of phosphate rock and silver also comes against a broader backdrop of efforts to maintain critical mineral trade and facilitate compliant exports, particularly in the rare-earth sector. China has taken steps to facilitate rare-earth exports within its regulatory framework. In December 2025, the Ministry of Commerce said some Chinese exporters had met the preliminary requirements for applying for general licenses for rare-earth-related items, and that applications had been received and approved. The ministry said the move followed policy briefings for exporters and the accumulation of export experience and compliance practices. China has also pledged to facilitate trade with the EU. On October 15, 2026, a MOFCOM spokesperson said that China was ready to continue to provide facilitation for the approval of rare earth export licenses to the EU, and also called on the EU side to reciprocally provide facilitation for specific priority licensing cases for China in the dual-use field. China's exports of rare-earth permanent magnets to the EU reached 2,454 tons in September, up 20.5 percent month-on-month and the highest level since February, according to media reports citing Chinese customs data. The increase does not by itself establish a direct link to licensing facilitation, but shows that trade in these materials continues amid regulatory scrutiny. Global critical mineral supply chains are highly interconnected, and both China and its trading partners benefit from stable supplies and predictable commercial arrangements, according to the analyst. Assessments of China's policies should consider actual trade flows, the processing of compliant export applications and concrete international cooperation, rather than relying on assumptions about political motives, according to Wu. At the same time, China has a responsibility to prevent controlled materials from being illegally exported or diverted to unauthorized uses, Wu said, noting that strict oversight of such activities is consistent with international practice and helps ensure that sensitive materials are used for legitimate purposes. At a regular press briefing in April, He Yadong, a MOFCOM spokesperson, said China remains committed to safeguarding the security and stability of global industrial and supply chains, fully taking into account reasonable civilian needs and concerns worldwide, including those of the US, and actively promoting and facilitating compliant trade. Export applications for rare earths that meet relevant requirements and are confirmed to be for civilian use would be approved in accordance with the law, according to the spokesperson. At the same time, Chinese authorities have repeatedly reaffirmed China's commitment to maintaining stable global critical mineral supply chains while strengthening export controls in line with international practices and fulfilling its non-proliferation obligations.

item.title: To understand the new 'Made in China' era, the West must shed prejudices: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 23:26:00
Dozens of UBTECH industrial humanoid robots carry out training tasks at a smart factory in the Qianwan New Area in Ningbo, East China's Zhejiang Province, on March 1, 2025. Photo: VCG The new face of "Made in China" is a transition from advantages of scale to systemic strengths, from cost competitiveness to innovation prowess, and from exporting goods to exporting capabilities. What the West truly needs to update is its entrenched mind-set of viewing China's development as a "zero-sum threat." On Thursday, Reuters published an article titled "Welcome to the new 'Made in China.'" Coining the term "new 'Made in China,'" the piece observed that Chinese manufacturing is expanding from cheap clothing, furniture, and toys into automobiles, complex machinery, high-end chemicals, and data center equipment. However, reading between the lines, the report remains accustomed to attributing China's competitiveness to subsidies, low prices, and "overcapacity." What does the new "Made in China" truly look like? Detaching oneself from an understanding of industrial ecosystems and competitive dynamics easily leads to the fallacy of "the blind men and the elephant" - mistaking a single leg for the entire creature. China's manufacturing sector is increasingly serving as the "factory of factories" supporting global industrial production. The strength of Chinese manufacturing is demonstrated not only in finished consumer products, but even more so in its capacity to provide critical equipment and foundational inputs for global production. Today, from precision control boards and specialized cabling to high-end machine tools and industrial robotics, Chinese manufacturing has become an indispensable component of global industrial upgrading and AI computing infrastructure. In the first three quarters of 2026, equipment manufacturing contributed nearly 90 percent of China's export growth. This vividly confirms a broader transition: China is steadily evolving from a provider of consumer goods into a pivotal supply-side hub for global productive capacity, while the bedrock of its competitiveness has upgraded from single-product price advantages to the systemic operational efficiency of an entire industrial ecosystem. The competitiveness of Chinese manufacturing has forged ahead through thorough market competition and continuous innovation. While subsidies may influence short-term costs, they can never replace a firm's long-term accumulation built through the process of market trial and error, process refinement, and rapid responsiveness to demand. Supported by an ultra-large domestic market, full-chain industrial integration, and a vast pool of engineering talent, new technologies in China swiftly transition from laboratory concepts to mass production before diffusing into adjacent sectors. Manufacturing competition itself has escalated into a contest of cross-industry technology transfer: perception and localization technologies developed for new-energy vehicles are spilling over into smart equipment, while the consumer robotics sector has pivoted from price wars toward competition over quality and brand reputation. Overseas consumer perceptions of Chinese products are similarly shifting - from "low price" to "technologically advanced and reliable." Brand premiums are increasingly determined by the speed of innovation and user acclaim. Dismissing the growth of Chinese manufacturing simply with terms like "subsidies" and "dumping" is not only factually incorrect, but also misreads the trajectory of global industry. Chinese manufacturing is evolving from exporting individual products to delivering comprehensive solutions. Research and development, design, manufacturing, digital operations and maintenance, and after-sales services are becoming deeply integrated. Industrial equipment manufacturers now provide customers with remote monitoring, preventive maintenance, and full lifecycle management, while logistics equipment companies integrate forklifts, warehousing systems, and digital platforms to improve customers' overall production efficiency. What Chinese companies deliver is no longer just individual pieces of hardware, but also the operation of entire production lines and support for complete production systems. The focus of value creation is consequently shifting toward system integration and long-term services. Meanwhile, China continues to advance institutional opening-up, making it clear that goods manufactured in China that meet domestic product standards are eligible for relevant government procurement support policies on an equal basis, regardless of whether their producers are domestic or foreign-invested enterprises. This latest round of upgrading is also opening up broader opportunities for global companies to participate in the Chinese market and leverage China's comprehensive industrial ecosystem. Trade barriers cannot override the economic forces that underpin industrial competitiveness. Tariffs may alter trade routes, but they cannot conjure up mature supply chains, a well-established pool of engineering talent, or deeply integrated industrial capabilities. Erecting barriers against Chinese intermediate goods and production equipment would instead raise the overall costs of industrial investment and technological upgrading in the countries imposing them. For countries determined to revitalize domestic manufacturing, shutting out cost-effective production inputs would not only fail to deliver the intended benefits but could also undermine the competitiveness of their domestic companies in third-country markets. The new face of "Made in China" is a transition from advantages of scale to systemic strengths, from cost competitiveness to innovation prowess, and from exporting goods to exporting capabilities. Every country has the right to develop its manufacturing sector, and every country has opportunities to participate in the international division of labor and benefit from technological progress. What the West truly needs to update is its entrenched mind-set of viewing China's development as a "zero-sum threat." Only by approaching competition with an open mind can countries create room for cooperation, and only by respecting objective economic laws can they turn the global trend of industrial upgrading into tangible opportunities for mutual benefit and win-win outcomes.

item.title: Why ASEAN won't buy Australian defence chief's claims on Chinese military
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 22:16:00
Australia's Defence Minister Richard Marles arrives before the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus in Cebu, Philippines, on October 29, 2026. Photo: VCG During the 20th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting in Manila, Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles once again trotted out the same old script: making unsubstantiated claims about "China's military buildup" and trying to use that as a pretext to push for closer ties among the so-called Squad - a small circle comprising the US, Japan, the Philippines and Australia. What Marles is essentially claiming boils down to this: China's defence development amounts to "applying pressure," while Australia's own military build-up is about "upholding the rules." These are blatant double standards. The regional "pressure" narrative reads more like a tailor‑made talking point for exclusive defence cliques. Yu Lei, a professor at the School of Northeast Asian Studies, Shandong University, noted that by making up claims about China's military, Marles is trying to force Southeast Asian nations to take sides. This seeks to erode the ASEAN-centric multilateral security architecture, replace Southeast Asia's open and inclusive regional order with bloc-driven confrontation and secure legitimacy for Australia's own military buildup. Yu further pointed out that Southeast Asian countries pursue an open, inclusive ASEAN-centered order and stand for safeguarding their autonomy and national interests through multilateral consultations. "The approach of making up threats while pushing for small military blocs will not only fail to win the support of Southeast Asia, but will also undermine Australia's sovereignty, interests and regional credibility." In fact, China has consistently adhered to the principles of amity, sincerity, mutual benefit and inclusiveness in its neighborhood diplomacy. It emphasizes the need to base its actions on the United Nations Charter and international law, opposes the instrumentalization and bloc-based use of "rules," and advocates building an Asia-Pacific community with a shared future through dialogue and cooperation, rather than "suppressing" other countries' legitimate rights to development through security alliances. China's defense spending accounts for less than 1.5 percent of its GDP. It is significantly lower than that of major military powers like the US, and is also below the global average. In contrast, Australia is vigorously advancing the AUKUS nuclear submarine program, investing tens of billions of Australian dollars to procure nuclear-powered submarines and long-range strike capabilities, expanding military bases in the north, and frequently conducting joint exercises with extra-regional forces in the South China Sea and waters surrounding the Philippines. It's clear who is putting pressure on regional peace and stability. What truly brings uncertainty to these waters are the frequent close-proximity activities of non-regional naval vessels and aircraft, as well as exclusionary defense arrangements intended for confrontation. Southeast Asian nations can clearly see who has been flip-flopping on the South China Sea issue, who is building bridges and roads in the Mekong subregion, who fuels militarization, who pushes for an exclusive restructuring of the regional security architecture, and who is committed to open and inclusive regional cooperation. For more than 30 years since China and ASEAN established their dialogue relationship, China has consistently participated in regional affairs with a constructive attitude, which in itself is the most concrete interpretation of "rules." Since 2020, China and ASEAN have consistently been each other's largest trading partners, and landmark projects such as the China-Laos Railway have delivered tangible benefits to local people. By contrast, security arrangements involving Australia often leave Southeast Asia with nothing but the roar of military exercises and the burden of defense spending. If Marles truly cares about the region, he should respect the right of countries to independently choose their own security paths, rather than trying to tell them what to do. In fact, it is clear Marles' rhetoric does not reflect any genuine concern for regional security, but rather anxiety over his own problematic defense agenda. It is becoming increasingly difficult to justify the hundreds of billions of Australian dollars invested in AUKUS nuclear submarines to the Australian people. Manufacturing claims about threats won't help with that.

item.title: GT Voice: SK shipbuilding's high-end edge hinges on Asian industrial collaboration
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 22:12:00
Visitors check out ship models at a booth during the Offshore Korea 2026 held in Busan, South Korea on October 14, 2026. Photo: VCG South Korea's shipbuilders posted third-quarter profits driven by high value vessels; however, sustaining their high end edge calls for regional industrial collaboration rather than yielding to external geopolitical demands that risk eroding long term industrial strengths. HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering announced on Wednesday that its third-quarter operating profit rose 37.3 percent year-on-year, driven by higher ship prices and strong earnings from its engine and offshore businesses, The Korea Herald reported. This strong performance is far from an isolated case. South Korea's three major shipbuilders all achieved relatively robust results in the third quarter of this year. Samsung Heavy Industries announced that its operating profit for the quarter increased by 42 percent year-on-year, bringing the combined operating profit of the three shipbuilders to 2.27 trillion won ($1.7 billion). This growth is attributed to continued revenue from high-value-added vessels, such as liquefied natural gas carriers. Behind these numbers lies the payoff of South Korea's shipbuilding sector in terms of high-value ship segments, a clear sign that it retains formidable competitiveness in premium shipbuilding markets. Yet the realization of the high-end ship dividend does not mean that competition will ease. High profitability tends to attract more resources into the high-end market. Global new ship orderbooks have seen China's share steadily rise amid intensifying market competition. If South Korea relies solely on the brand and technological reputation it has built up while neglecting supply-chain efficiency and sustained research and development, its high-end edge could be gradually squeezed. Holding the leading position requires more than winning high-priced orders; it demands stable delivery, consolidation of core supporting industries, cultivation of technical talent, and the continuous creation of new product advantages. This is precisely why South Korea's shipbuilding sector needs stable regional industrial collaboration more than ever. After decades of growth, Asia's shipbuilding industrial chain has formed a close, sophisticated division of labor that cannot be easily severed. The interconnected ecosystem spans parts supply, materials and equipment, vessel design technology, and specialized skilled personnel. Even as companies across the region compete fiercely for new orders, they can still identify shared interests in supply chain coordination, technical exchanges, and alignment of industry standards. To channel all their resources into technological upgrades and consolidate their hold on high-end segments, South Korea's shipbuilders need the support of the Asian industrial ecosystem. The coexistence of competition and cooperation has become a reality for Asia's shipbuilding landscape. Any attempt to break these deeply integrated industrial ties will ultimately undermine South Korea's own core competitiveness. At this critical juncture, persistent efforts by the US to poach South Korean shipbuilding capacity and pull it into its own industrial arrangements deserve particular vigilance. Such "cooperation" may appear to bring new orders and market access, but if its essence is to steer South Korean firms to channel their capital, technology, talent, and key production capacity toward serving America's industrial goals, South Korea must carefully assess the long-term costs. Shipbuilding is not a single factory that can be relocated at will. Its competitiveness is built on decades of accumulated supplier networks, engineering expertise, and seamless industrial collaboration. Restructuring production outside this established system will not only drive up costs across supply chains, personnel training, and operational coordination, but also divert resources that should be dedicated to South Korea's own industrial upgrading, potentially allowing its clearly laid-out development roadmap to be hijacked by external strategic priorities. Whether South Korea's shipbuilding sector can hold onto today's achievements will depend entirely on its willingness to keep innovating amid intensifying competition and seizing the initiative while deepening mutually beneficial regional cooperation. By expanding pragmatic regional collaboration, South Korea can turn its current profit into a solid foundation for long-term growth. Advancing regional cooperation is a key way for South Korea to translate today's profits into a foundation for lasting growth, rather than gradually consuming the industrial advantages in the course of catering to external geopolitical demands.

item.title: Reconnaissance setup boosts carrier situational awareness: Chinese expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 22:06:00
A WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance unmanned aerial vehicle Photo: Screenshot from the military channel of the CCTV News As the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy's Liaoning carrier group continues the training in the western Pacific, Japan's Defense Ministry Joint Staff has claimed it has spotted not only vessel movements but also military aircraft activities, mostly those of reconnaissance planes. Against the backdrop of a US-Japan joint exercise, a Chinese expert said the reconnaissance aircraft may be providing situational awareness and intelligence support for the carrier group, while Japan's sensationalism surrounding these reports is driven more by political convenience than by genuine security concerns. On Thursday, when asked to comment on reports that Japan had released data showing that its Air Self-Defense Force had scrambled 442 times in response to Chinese and Russian military aircraft from April to September this year, an increase of nearly 70 percent from the same period last year, including 285 scrambles in response to Chinese military aircraft and 152 in response to Russian military aircraft, as well as the Japanese defense minister's claim that joint China-Russia patrols were a "show of force" against Japan, Chinese Defense Ministry spokesperson Senior Colonel Zhang Xiaogang said that Japan was using its usual tactics to hype up the so-called security threats in its neighborhood. This only served to confirm Japan's dangerous practice of frequently surveilling and harassing legitimate activities conducted by China and Russia, and exposed Japan's tendency to frighten itself with imagined threats, Zhang Xiaogang said. He urged Japan to stop playing such deceptive tricks and refrain from creating and hyping up tensions. On Wednesday evening, Japan's Defense Ministry Joint Staff claimed that a PLA BZK-005 reconnaissance drone and a Y-9 intelligence-gathering aircraft had passed through the Miyako Strait into the Pacific that day. Later on the same day, a Y-9 patrol aircraft flew from the southwest of the Danjo Islands in the Nagasaki Prefecture toward waters northwest of Okinawa Island. Similar monitoring was reported in the preceding days. On October 19, for instance, the Joint Staff claimed a PLA BZK-005 and a Y-9 flew from the East China Sea through the Miyako Strait into the Pacific, circled over the ocean and returned. The same day, a PLA TB-001 reconnaissance/strike drone flew from the East China Sea through the area between Yonaguni Island and Taiwan island into the Pacific. Reports on the Y-9 have been the most frequent during this period, six days of notices on the aircraft, according to the Joint Staff's website. These alleged sightings of Chinese aerial reconnaissance assets have come since the PLA Navy announced on October 14 that it had dispatched the Liaoning carrier group to conduct training in the western Pacific. The PLA Navy said the deployment was a routine training mission carried out as part of the country's annual plan, aimed at testing and improving combat-oriented training and continuously enhancing the ability to fulfill missions. It complies with relevant international law and practice and does not target any specific country or target. Meanwhile, a large US-Japan exercise was held from October 19 to 29. The large-scale "Keen Sword 27" military exercise involved more than 50,000 personnel from the Japan Self-Defense Forces and US forces, the Kyodo News has reported. Zhang Junshe, a Chinese military affairs expert, said that with the Liaoning's far-sea training and the US-Japan exercise overlapping, the Chinese reconnaissance aircraft may, to some extent, be providing situational awareness and intelligence support for the carrier group. This multi-layered reconnaissance setup reflects the PLA Navy's approach to system-based far-sea training and joint operations, Zhang Junshe told the Global Times. It is building a far-sea comprehensive support and situational awareness system, improving the carrier group's sustained combat capability and information advantage in complex waters far from the base. Complementary reconnaissance platforms also enable three-dimensional, real-time battlefield awareness, improving information acquisition and responsiveness in complex electromagnetic environments and high-intensity confrontations. At the same time, it tests and improves system-based combat effectiveness in realistic conditions, reflecting a combat-oriented training approach, Zhang Junshe said. Separately, a CCTV News report on Sunday commented on Japan's footage of a Chinese WZ-7 high-altitude reconnaissance drone, shot from below, indicating a significant altitude gap between the filming aircraft and the WZ-7. "The drone's maximum flight altitude is about 19,000 to 20,000 meters. If Japan can only look up to observe, locate and track the aircraft, it means Japanese assets cannot reach that altitude. At its maximum height, the drone's reconnaissance, early warning signal transmission and connectivity can reach a new level. China's air and sea advantages are being rapidly established in the relevant waters," military commentator Du Wenlong was quoted by CCTV as saying. On October 14, Japan said that afternoon, a Y-9 operated between the waters southwest of the Danjo Islands and waters northwest of Okinawa. Additionally, a PLA WZ-7 reconnaissance drone flew over the East China Sea. Zhang Junshe said that Japan's frequent releases on Chinese ships and aircraft amount to making a fuss out of nothing. The primary aim is to justify higher defense budgets, military expansion and remilitarization; the second is to manufacture regional tension and a favorable atmosphere for US-Japan military coordination in the Asia-Pacific.

item.title: Steinmeier's visit highlights China-Germany industrial links as Merz sends mixed signals
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 21:46:00
During his visit to Peking University in Beijing on October 29, 2026, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier poses for photos with students and engages them in a game of table tennis. Photo: Li Hao/Global Times German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's ongoing state visit to China has put the spotlight on the deep industrial ties and innovation cooperation between the two countries, even as trade frictions and remarks by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz during a separate Asian tour have sent contrasting signals about Berlin's approach to Beijing. Chinese analysts said Steinmeier's visit presents an opportunity to strengthen economic cooperation and rebuild mutual trust. However, they warned that politicizing trade disputes and bringing Asian security issues into Germany's China policy could undercut those efforts, undermining bilateral relations and Germany's long-term interests. On Thursday, Steinmeier received an honorary professorship from Peking University in Beijing and delivered a speech on China-Germany relations, according to the dpa German Press Agency. The German president's October 27-31 state visit marks his first trip to China in nearly eight years. During a stop in Hefei, East China's Anhui Province, on Tuesday, he toured Volkswagen's largest research and development center outside Germany and experienced intelligent electric vehicles developed locally. Steinmeier is scheduled to hold talks with the Chinese president, while the Chinese premier and top legislator will also meet with him, according to China's Foreign Ministry. The visit has raised expectations among German businesses and industry representatives for deeper bilateral economic ties and closer cooperation in technological innovation. On Wednesday, Volkswagen announced that its Compact Main Platform (CMP) and China Electronic Architecture (CEA), developed in Hefei with Chinese partners, would underpin next-generation vehicles for Global South markets, starting with South America by the end of the decade, according to Reuters. "China is a key innovation engine for the Volkswagen Group - and increasingly a product and tech hub for our global markets," Volkswagen Group CEO Oliver Blume said in a statement. "We call it in China, and beyond." Such deep industrial integration reflects market-driven cooperation and has become an important source of German industrial competitiveness, Chen Hong, director of the Country and Region Studies Institute at the School of Foreign Languages, East China Normal University, told the Global Times on Thursday. China is no longer merely a major market for German products but has also become an important partner in technological innovation and industrial upgrading, particularly in electric vehicles and intelligent manufacturing, Chen said. However, the strength of these commercial ties contrasts with a more complicated political climate. Germany and the broader EU face mounting domestic economic pressures, while calls to reduce "dependence" on China and tighten trade restrictions have grown louder. China-EU trade differences should be handled through professional negotiations, rather than cast as ideological or national security disputes. Such an approach risks undermining mutual trust, said Jiang Feng, a senior researcher at the Shanghai International Studies University and president of the Shanghai Regional Studies Association. China has repeatedly emphasized that it is not the source of the problems facing the EU, but a partner in finding solutions, Chinese Commerce Ministry spokesperson Huang Ling said on Thursday, responding to reports that the EU was considering extending trade arrangements reached with China over hybrid vehicles to other sectors, including chemicals. However, China firmly opposes any form of protectionism involving the abuse of trade defense instruments. "If the EU insists on imposing discriminatory restrictions on Chinese products, China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own interests and the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies," Huang said. While German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier visits China, Chancellor Friedrich Merz is touring Singapore, Japan and South Korea, pursuing a more China-wary agenda that underscores the growing complexity of Berlin's approach to Beijing, according to media reports. Merz met Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Tokyo on Wednesday, where the two leaders agreed to deepen cooperation in areas including security, economic security and advanced technologies, according to the Japan Times. At a press conference, Merz expressed concern over rising tensions in the Indo-Pacific, particularly in the Taiwan Straits, claiming that the UN Charter's prohibition on the use of force also applies to the region and urging all sides to exercise utmost caution, according to the German government's official website. Merz's remarks during his Asian tour could diminish the positive signals emerging from Steinmeier's China visit, erode mutual trust and introduce new uncertainties into regional security, Chinese analysts said, adding that deep industrial ties underscore the need for dialogue rather than confrontation. Jiang pointed to both countries' historical responsibilities for World War II and the suffering inflicted on Asian nations by militarism, warning that Merz's remarks could largely undercut the positive signals sent by the German president's visit to China. "Germany should recognize that the Taiwan question concerns China's core interests and should not become a political instrument for strengthening military cooperation with Japan," Chen said. During his visit to Singapore on Tuesday, Merz warned against full economic decoupling from China but called for reducing what he described as "unhealthy, one-sided dependencies" in supply chains, technology and raw materials, Reuters reported. Responding to Merz's remarks, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun urged Germany and the EU to stay objective and rational and work in the same direction with China, so that the two sides can resolve differences and disputes through dialogue and consultation, keep global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded, and provide more certainty for cooperation between their business communities.

item.title: HKSAR housing chief resigns over deadly Wang Fuk Court fire; CE John Lee announces accountability probe and reforms following inquiry report
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 19:35:00
Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Chief Executive John Lee and other officials bowed and apologized at a press conference on October 29, 2026, as the investigation report into the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po was released. Photo: Screenshot of a RTHK report Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Secretary for Housing Winnie Ho had resigned to take political responsibility for the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po, which claimed 168 lives in November 2025, HKSAR Chief Executive John Lee announced on Thursday as the government released an independent committee's investigation report into the tragedy, according to local media reports. Lee said at a press conference on Thursday afternoon that he had accepted Ho's resignation, although no personal misconduct had been found. Ho offered her resignation during a meeting with Lee on Wednesday, and HKSAR Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong would take over her duties, according to media reports. Before the press conference began, Lee and other senior government officials bowed to the public in apology over the tragedy. Lee expressed deep sorrow over the fire, which killed 168 people and affected 1,984 families, saying that the it had brought immense grief to the victims' families and sadness to society as a whole, according to RTHK. Lee said the independent committee's report identified inadequacies and shortcomings in the responsibilities and the oversight exercised by four government bodies in relation to fire risks associated with renovation works at Wang Fuk Court, namely the Housing Bureau's Independent Checking Unit (ICU), the Buildings Department, the Fire Services Department and the Labour Department. He announced the launch of the Administrative Responsibility Two-tier Investigation Mechanism under Heads of Department Accountability System (HoD Accountability System).The case will be referred to the Public Service Commission for investigation in accordance with its investigation regulations, with the process to be completed within three months. The investigation will examine whether relevant personnel had neglected their duties or violated departmental regulations and civil service rules, and make recommendations on possible disciplinary action or administrative sanctions based on the findings. As part of the reforms, Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong announced that a new public housing building control unit would be established in November to replace the Housing Bureau's ICU. The new unit will introduce a new regulatory system and establish dedicated project teams, with designated officers proactively contacting owners' corporations to provide assistance and one-stop communication services to residents. Secretary for Justice Paul Lam said he supported the committee's recommendation to amend the Competition Ordinance to criminalize bid-rigging and other serious anti-competitive conduct, including price-fixing. The proposed penalties could include up to 10 years in prison and a fine of up to HK$10 million, three times the proceeds, or 50 percent of local turnover. The fire broke out at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on November 26, 2025, becoming one of the deadliest residential fires in Hong Kong's history since 1948, according to a transcript from an evidential hearing held on 19 March 2026 by the Independent Committee investigating the fire. The independent committee found that the fire was most likely caused by a heat source, probably a lit cigarette, that ignited combustible materials, while unsafe construction materials, including non-fire-retardant scaffolding nets, and human errors or negligence contributed to the rapid spread of the blaze and heavy casualties, according to RTHK. The independent committee submitted its report to Lee on October 22 after holding 30 days of evidential hearings and hearing oral evidence from 80 factual and expert witnesses, according to the HKSAR government. The committee was tasked with examining the causes of the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po and related issues. The government has pledged comprehensive reforms in areas including the supervision of building maintenance works, building management and the regulation of fire service installations. Willy Kin Chi Fu, president of the Association for the Promotion of Rule of Law, Education and Technology, told the Global Times on Thursday that he supported the government's decision to release the independent committee's report, Lee's public apology, Ho's resignation to take political responsibility and the launch of investigations into regulatory shortcomings involving the four government bodies. Public accountability and political responsibility are necessary responses to the tragedy, he said. Fu noted that the report put forward 120 recommendations to address systemic loopholes in building maintenance and renovation works. He highlighted the government's reform measures, including efforts to criminalize bid-rigging, establish a dedicated building maintenance support body to assist property owners, strengthen penalties under the Buildings Ordinance, and set up a steering committee led by the Chief Secretary for Administration to oversee the implementation of reforms. The weight of the 120 recommendations shows that the problems were not merely the result of individual officials' mistakes, but reflected deep-rooted shortcomings," Fu said. He stressed that supporting accountability also means supporting every subsequent step toward implementing the reforms. "Only by ensuring that these reforms are effectively implemented can we provide the most responsible response to the loss of 168 lives," he added. The HKSAR government's release of the independent committee's report on the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire, along with its decisions on criminal accountability, administrative accountability and political responsibility, and its proposed systematic reforms, demonstrates its commitment to putting people first, upholding the rule of law, confronting problems and improving governance, the State Council's Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office commented on Thursday. These measures will help strengthen social unity, build consensus on reforms and advance Hong Kong's transition from stability to prosperity, it said.

item.title: China's longest metro loop line now operational in Wuhan, with transfers to 18 lines
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 15:57:00
China's longest subway loop line, Line 12 of Wuhan Metro in Central China's Hubei Province, fully opens on October 29, 2026. Photo: Screenshot from China Media Group China's longest subway loop line, Line 12 of Wuhan Metro in Central China's Hubei Province, fully opened on Thursday. With a total length of 59.9 kilometers and 37 underground stations, the line provides interchange access to 18 existing and planned metro lines. The line runs through seven central urban districts, including Qiaokou, Jianghan and Jiang'an. It connects the two major railway hubs of Hankou Station and Wuchang Station. The whole journey through the loop would take about 96 minutes. It was opened in two phases. Phase 1, spanning 35.3 kilometers, went into operation on May 1. The newly opened Phase 2 extends 24.6 kilometers and completes the full loop. The line crosses under the Yangtze River twice and the Han River once. It features one of China's longest cross-river metro shield tunnels, and the builders overcame many construction challenges, including high water pressure, complex mixed strata, and long-distance underwater shield tunneling. It serves as a demonstration project for both cluster construction of cross-river metro tunnels and large-loop rail transit development. The line also features Grade of Automation 4 level fully automated operation, the highest grade of automatic train operation in rail transit. Each morning, the trains wake up automatically, run self-diagnostics, and roll out of depots on their own. During service, they perform automatic turnbacks and station stops. Late at night, after operations end, they plan their own routes back to the depot and go into sleep mode. This entire "wake up-go to work-clock off-go to sleep" cycle requires no manual intervention, and the control center can take remote control at any time. The trains have been specially trained. During peak hours, they automatically adjust headways, and in emergencies they can independently plan detours, taking on-time performance and emergency response to a new level. The opening of Line 12 breaks the natural barriers of the Yangtze and Han rivers that have long constrained cross-river commutes. It will also support the development of a comprehensive transport hub in Wuhan city. Global Times

item.title: China opposes US blacklisting of three Chinese firms over so-called 'forced labor' accusations, vows to safeguard interests
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29 15:36:00
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun Two Chinese ministries on Thursday expressed strong dissatisfaction with and firm opposition to the US decision to add three Chinese genomics entities to the so-called "Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List," vowing to take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard the lawful rights and interests of Chinese enterprises. "The US has been spreading disinformation about Xinjiang and using so-called "forced labor" as false pretext to suppress Chinese enterprises. China deplores and firmly opposes the move," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Thursday. The remarks came as the US added BGI Genomics Co Ltd, MGI Tech Co Ltd, and Shenzhen BGI Technology Co Ltd to the "Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List," a move that bans imports from the three companies, according to a statement posted by the US Department of Homeland Security on its website on Wednesday. The so-called "forced labor" is a huge lie propagated by anti-China forces to destabilize Xinjiang, smear China and curb its development, Guo said. He noted that China urges the US to stop interfering in China's internal affairs and curbing China's development in the name of human rights. China will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard the lawful rights and interests of Chinese enterprises. "There is no 'forced labor' in China, and people of all ethnic groups in Xinjiang enjoy freedom and equality in employment, with their labor rights and interests effectively protected by law," a spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) said Thursday. The MOFCOM spokesperson noted that the US had recently added a large number of Chinese entities to the same list. China has lodged solemn representations with the US side and taken resolute countermeasures. Disregarding China's firm opposition, the US has continued to impose new sanctions, this time targeting Chinese biomedical technology companies, the spokesperson said. Such actions run counter to the consensus reached by the two countries' heads of state, seriously undermine the stability of China-US economic and trade relations, and are contrary to humanitarian principles, the spokesperson added. The three companies involved have also stated their positions on the matter. They strongly opposed the US government's decision. "We firmly reject all allegations. BGI Group has not engaged in any form of forced labor. BGI Group strictly complies with applicable laws and regulations in China and the countries and regions where it operates, and respects internationally recognized principles concerning human rights and labor standards. We firmly oppose all forms of forced labor," BGI Group said in a statement sent to the Global Times on Thursday. BGI Genomics expressed strong opposition to the US allegation in a similar statement on Thursday. MGI Tech Co Ltd stressed in a statement sent to the Global Times that "We firmly reject the allegations, which we believe are unfounded and inconsistent with the facts." Jia Chunyang, research fellow at Development Research Center of the State Council, told the Global Times on Thursday that the "forced labor" accusation serves merely as a pretext: The true purpose is to destabilize the Xinjiang region and disrupt its development. "The US moves may seem high-sounding, but in essence are underhanded tricks that cannot stand up to scrutiny. They will only create obstacles for China-US economic and trade relations, undermine the strategic consensus reached between the two countries' leaders, and create new uncertainties in the bilateral relationship," Jia said.
